title: Geometric-point projection morphism agrees with the constant-section projection morphism
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $Z$ any scheme and $h:Z\to s$ a morphism. Use ordinary derived tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [def-kun-derived-tensor] on the unbounded small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $S_D$ and $C_s$ be the normalized monoidal geometric-stalk/constant equivalence [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants], and let $\beta:S_D Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z$ and $\gamma:h^{-1}C_s\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ be the canonical comparisons [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-sections-adjunction]. For any $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$ and $M\in D(\mathbf Z)$, the following square commutes:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
S_D(Rh_*E\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}C_s M)&\xrightarrow{S_D(\mathrm{PF}_h(E,C_s M))}&S_D Rh_*(E\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}h^{-1}C_s M)\\
\downarrow\alpha&&\downarrow\delta\\
R\Gamma_ZE\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}M&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{Z,\mathbf Z}(E,M)}&R\Gamma_Z(E\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}C_Z M).
\end{array}$$
Here the upper projection morphism is [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and the lower one is [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. The left vertical isomorphism $\alpha$ is the monoidal comparison for $S_D$, followed by $\beta_E$ and inverse to $M\to S_D C_s M$. The right vertical isomorphism $\delta$ is $\beta_{E\otimes^L h^{-1}C_sM}$ followed by $R\Gamma_Z(1_E\otimes^L\gamma_M)$. This is an equality of canonical morphisms, with no assertion that either horizontal morphism is invertible and with no properness, boundedness or torsion assumption.

proof.text: Write $F=h^{-1}$, $H=Rh_*$, $S=S_D$, $C=C_s$, $L=C_Z$, $R=R\Gamma_Z$, and $u:1\to SC$, $v:CS\to1$ for the equivalence unit and counit. All tensors below are derived over $\mathbf Z$, and $c^T:T(A\otimes B)\to TA\otimes TB$ denotes a comonoidal constraint. Let $a:s_{\mathrm{Et}}\to *$ and $b:Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\to *$ be the terminal ringed-topos morphisms, with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$ on the one-object point site. Their inverse images are the constant-sheaf functors, and $b=ah$ with pullback comparison $\gamma:FC\to L$. The adjunction for $a$ is $C\dashv S$, with unit $u$ and counit $v$, by [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. The adjunction for $b$ is $L\dashv R$ by [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. The comparison of the composite right adjoint $SH$ with $R$ is precisely $\beta$: [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-sections-adjunction] specifies it by the counit equation, rather than by an arbitrary isomorphism of functors. Thus these are the canonical comparisons to which the ringed-topos composition formula applies.

proof.text:
For $A\in D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$ put
$$a_{A,M}=(1_{SA}\otimes u_M^{-1})\circ c^S_{A,CM}:S(A\otimes CM)\xrightarrow{\sim}SA\otimes M.$$
Let $\pi_a(A,M):SA\otimes M\to S(A\otimes CM)$ be the counit-defined projection map for $C\dashv S$. Its adjunct is $(v_A\otimes1_{CM})\circ c^C_{SA,M}$ by the projection-map definition. Monoidality of $v$ and the triangle identity $v_{CM}\circ C(u_M)=1_{CM}$ give the three-line calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
v_{A\otimes CM}\circ C(a_{A,M}^{-1})
&=v_{A\otimes CM}\circ C((c^S_{A,CM})^{-1})\circ C(1_{SA}\otimes u_M)\\
&=(v_A\otimes v_{CM})\circ c^C_{SA,SCM}\circ C(1_{SA}\otimes u_M)\\
&=(v_A\otimes1_{CM})\circ c^C_{SA,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The left side is the adjunct of $a_{A,M}^{-1}$; injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore proves $\pi_a(A,M)=a_{A,M}^{-1}$. This uses the specified monoidal unit and counit of the equivalence, without changing tensor normalizations.

proof.text:
Apply the composition identity of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] to the ringed-topos morphisms $Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\xrightarrow h s_{\mathrm{Et}}\xrightarrow a *$, the object $E$ and the coefficient complex $M$. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary unbounded module complexes and impose no properness or invertibility assumption. Set $A=HE$, $N=E\otimes FCM$, $B=E\otimes LM$, $q=1_E\otimes\gamma_M:N\to B$, and $P=\mathrm{PF}_h(E,CM)$. The three projection maps in the cited identity are exactly $P$, $\pi_a(A,M)$ and $\mathrm{PF}_{Z,\mathbf Z}(E,M)$ by their counit-adjunct definitions. Restoring the canonical right-adjoint comparisons suppressed in that identity gives
$$\mathrm{PF}_{Z,\mathbf Z}(E,M)\circ(\beta_E\otimes1_M)
=R(q)\circ\beta_N\circ S(P)\circ\pi_a(A,M).$$
In particular the target comparison is $R(q)\circ\beta_N$, and the source comparison is $\beta_E\otimes1_M$. These are the specific $\gamma$ and $\beta$ fixed in step 1 by the constant pullback and the counit equation; the cited lemma asserts the formula with canonical pullback and direct-image composition comparisons, so no compatibility is being inferred from the bare existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map (counit-defined projection); Tags 07A4 and 07A6 (canonical tensor and adjunction comparisons); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F0F, final geometric-fibre formula.

proof.text:
Substitute $\pi_a(A,M)=a_{A,M}^{-1}$ from step 2 into the equation of step 3 and precompose by $a_{A,M}$. Since $\alpha=(\beta_E\otimes1_M)\circ a_{A,M}$ and $\delta=R(q)\circ\beta_N$ by the statement, cancellation gives
$$\mathrm{PF}_{Z,\mathbf Z}(E,M)\circ\alpha=\delta\circ S(P).$$
This is precisely the asserted square. Only $a_{A,M}$, which is an isomorphism of normalized tensor constraints and the equivalence unit, was inverted. Neither projection morphism was inverted. All objects remain in the unbounded ordinary integer-coefficient derived categories throughout.

lean.note: GeometricPointProjectionSquare is a transparent formula for the original square, universally quantified over E and M. The theorem specializes its functors, monoidal stalk, invertible germ unit, canonical beta and gamma, and the two recorded counit-defined projection transformations; it assumes none of their compatibility. The lower transformation is exactly the one evaluated by constantDerivedProjectionMap.
